title: About — Why We Stopped Leading With Websites | ALL8 WEBWORKS
description: ALL8 WEBWORKS is an owner-led practice that finds where opportunities are lost between a search and a won job — and fixes the costliest part.

hero.subtitle: Not because websites stopped mattering — but because the data kept showing us they usually weren't the reason a business wasn't booking enough work.
hero.subtitleStrong: So we changed what we sell.

shift.title: The Job Description Changed. The Work Didn't.

cards.title: A business needs a website. We build the website.
cards.body: The project starts with a deliverable that was decided before anyone looked at the business. It launches, it looks good, and whether it produces more work is largely left to chance.

cards.title: A business needs more work. We find out why it isn't happening.
cards.body: The project starts with a diagnosis. Sometimes the answer is a website. Often it's search visibility, or the phone, or what happens to a lead three days after it arrives.

story: The change didn't come from a strategy session. It came from watching a client's numbers after we'd done what we were hired to do.

An established service business came to us with weak local search visibility. We rebuilt the site, improved their Google Business Profile, built dedicated pages for the services they actually wanted, and — this is the part that mattered — **added tracking so we could see what happened next.**

The visibility work performed. Page-one rankings for the targeted service pages, top local visibility for high-intent searches, appearances in Google's AI-generated answers, and a 76% year-over-year increase in Business Profile website clicks.

Then the tracking showed us something we hadn't been hired to look at. **More people were calling. Not all of those calls were being answered, and the ones that came in as form submissions weren't consistently followed up.**
shift.pullQuote: We had successfully fixed a problem that was no longer the biggest one.
storyAfter: Without the tracking, nobody would have known. The obvious next move would have been more SEO — more visibility poured into a stage that couldn't hold it.

That's the whole argument for how we work now. Getting found is one stage of five. If you only ever sell the first stage, you can do genuinely good work and still leave your client's real problem untouched.

founder.title: You Work With the Person Doing the Work
paragraphs: ALL8 is intentionally small. Strategy, implementation and optimization stay close to the person actually doing the work — without layers of account managers or handoffs.

That's also why the diagnosis comes before the proposal. There's no sales team here carrying a website quota, so the recommendation can be whatever the evidence supports — including telling you your website is fine and the problem is somewhere else.

Matt works directly with service businesses to find where opportunities are being lost, then connects the website, search visibility, calls, follow-up and reporting around one goal: turning more of them into customers.

principles.title: Four Things We Don't Bend On

items.title: Diagnosis before proposal
items.body: We look at the whole path — search, site, forms, phone, follow-up, tracking — before recommending anything. If the highest-impact fix is something we don't sell, we'll say so.

items.title: Your accounts, your data
items.body: Your domain, content, ad accounts, analytics and customer records stay in your name. Recurring services are identified clearly, and website code transfer follows the published subscription terms.

items.title: Measured, not asserted
items.body: Call and form tracking goes in early, so the work can be judged on leads and sources rather than impressions and adjectives. It also tells us when we've fixed the wrong thing.

items.title: Use what's already working
items.body: If your team already uses a CRM, quoting tool or scheduling software, we connect to it instead of replacing it. New tools get recommended when the current ones genuinely can't do the job.

who.title: Businesses Where a Lead Becomes a Conversation
who.subtitle: Not e-commerce, not apps. Service businesses, where an opportunity turns into a call, a consultation, a quote or a booked job — and where losing one is expensive.
who.note: The trade matters less than the shape of the business. If customers find you through search or referral, call or request a quote, and then wait on a human to respond — the same five stages apply, and they fail in the same places.
